mainTopic: The cries of the עזרה, the downfall of יששכר איש כפר ברקאי, and the closing of מסכת כריתות
overview: This amud finishes a ברייתא listing the 'cries' that the עזרה (Temple courtyard) let out about certain כהנים. The second cry ends by noting that, because of one כהן, sacrificial meat was never left over. The third cry welcomes אלישמע בן פיכאי, a student of פנחס, to serve as כהן גדול. The fourth cry demands that יששכר איש כפר ברקאי be thrown out, because he wrapped his hands in silk during the עבודה. The גמרא tells how ינאי המלך asked him whether goat or lamb is better. יששכר answered with a dismissive hand gesture, and he ended up losing both hands, which רב יוסף calls a fitting punishment. רב אשי and רבינא show that his answer was wrong anyway, since both the משנה and the פסוקים treat lambs and goats as equal. The מסכת closes with the teaching that תלמידי חכמים increase peace in the world, followed by the הדרן ending מסכת כריתות.

steps.title: The end of the second cry: no leftover meat
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא finishes describing the כהן of the second cry. Because he ate so much, sacrificial meat was never left over in the עזרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He even ate birds for dessert. People said that in all his days, no sacrificial meat was ever left over in the courtyard.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא is finishing a sentence that started just before this point, about a כהן who ate huge amounts of sacrificial meat. It ends with the result: in his lifetime there was never any נותר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נותר is sacrificial meat left past its time, which must be burned instead of eaten. This כהן's huge appetite meant the קדשים were always eaten in time and never wasted, which is why the עזרה cried out about him.

keyTerms.meaning: Dessert, the end of the meal
Sacrificial meat left past the time it may be eaten
The courtyard of the בית המקדש

phrases.english: for dessert.
They said: all his days
there was never leftover meat in the courtyard.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמרו כל ימיו לא היה נותר בעזרה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the second cry, which started before this part of the text.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Because of this כהן, sacrificial meat was never left over in the עזרה.

steps.title: The third cry: let אלישמע בן פיכאי serve
steps.stepSummary: The עזרה calls for its gates to open so that אלישמע בן פיכאי, a student of פנחס, can enter and serve as כהן גדול.
steps.simpleTranslation: The third cry was: 'Lift up your heads, O gates, and let אלישמע בן פיכאי, the student of פנחס, come in and serve as כהן גדול.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives the third cry of the עזרה. This one is praise: it calls for a worthy כהן to come in and serve as כהן גדול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The cry uses the words of a פסוק to welcome someone worthy. Calling him a 'student of פנחס' means he follows in the path of that great, zealous כהן, so he is fit for כהונה גדולה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Lift up your heads, O gates' (a פסוק)
The office of the כהן גדול (High Priest)

phrases.english: The third cry:
Lift up your heads, O gates,
and let Elishama ben Pikai enter,
the student of Pinchas,
and serve as High Priest.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next cry in the list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אלישמע בן פיכאי is worthy to serve as כהן גדול.

steps.title: The fourth cry: throw out יששכר איש כפר ברקאי
steps.stepSummary: The עזרה calls for יששכר איש כפר ברקאי to be thrown out, because he honors himself and disgraces holy things.
steps.simpleTranslation: The fourth cry was: 'Open the gates and throw out יששכר איש כפר ברקאי, who honors himself and disgraces the holy things of Heaven.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives the fourth cry, and this one is a condemnation. Instead of welcoming a כהן, the gates should open to send this one out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Notice the contrast: the third cry opened the gates to bring someone in, and this cry opens them to push someone out. His sin is described as caring about his own honor more than the honor of קדשי שמים.

keyTerms.meaning: Things made holy for Heaven (sacrifices and Temple items)

phrases.english: The fourth cry:
Open the gates
and take out Yissachar of Kfar Barkai,
who honors himself
and disgraces the holy things of Heaven.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The next cry in the list, now a negative one that contrasts with the third.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: יששכר איש כפר ברקאי should be thrown out for honoring himself and disgracing קדשים.

steps.title: What did יששכר actually do?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what יששכר did that earned him this condemnation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to ask what his actual behavior was. It is setting up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא only gave a general accusation. The גמרא wants the concrete action behind 'honors himself and disgraces קדשים'.

keyTerms.meaning: What would he do? (asking about a regular habit)

phrases.english: What would he do?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the details behind the fourth cry.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The specific behavior that made יששכר 'honor himself and disgrace קדשים'.

steps.title: He wrapped silk on his hands during the service
steps.stepSummary: יששכר would cover his hands with silk and only then do the Temple service.
steps.simpleTranslation: He would wrap silk over his hands and then do the service.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: he put silk over his hands while doing the עבודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He kept his own hands clean and comfortable while handling the קרבנות, as if the holy work was beneath him. That is exactly 'honoring himself' while 'disgracing קדשי שמים'.

phrases.english: He would wrap silk over his hands
and perform the service.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of what he did.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He wrapped silk on his hands while doing the עבודה, protecting himself instead of honoring the holy service.

steps.title: What happened to יששכר in the end?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what finally became of יששכר איש כפר ברקאי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how his story ended. This sets up the story that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now that we know his sin, the גמרא wants to show the result. The answer is a story about how he was punished.

keyTerms.meaning: What became of him? (literally 'what came up for him')

phrases.english: What became of him?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After explaining his sin, the גמרא turns to what happened to him.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What finally happened to יששכר איש כפר ברקאי.

steps.title: ינאי המלך and the queen argue about goat and lamb
steps.stepSummary: ינאי המלך and the queen argued over whether goat or lamb meat tastes better, and decided to ask יששכר, the כהן גדול, who knew food well.
steps.simpleTranslation: ינאי המלך and the queen were sitting together. The king said goat meat is better, and the queen said lamb is better. They said, 'Let's ask יששכר איש כפר ברקאי, since he is the כהן גדול and knows his dishes well.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins the story that answers what happened to יששכר. The king and queen have a food argument and decide to call him in as the expert.
steps.deeperAnalysis: As כהן גדול he ate many kinds of sacrificial meat, so he was seen as an expert on taste. This sets up the meeting where his attitude toward קדשים will be exposed, which steps 8 and 9 describe.

keyTerms.meaning: He knows well, is an expert in
A pot; here, cooking and dishes

phrases.english: King Yannai and the queen
were sitting.
The king said: goat is better,
and the queen said: lamb is better.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַרוּ: נְשַׁיְּילֵיהּ לְיִשָּׂשׂכָר אִישׁ כְּפַר בַּרְקַאי,
phrases.english: They said: let us ask Yissachar of Kfar Barkai,
since he is the High Priest
and he knows dishes well.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the story that answers what happened to יששכר.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The story begins: the king and queen call יששכר to settle their argument about goat and lamb meat. Steps 8 and 9 tell the rest of the story.

steps.title: יששכר answers that lamb is better
steps.stepSummary: Asked which meat is better, יששכר answers that if goat were better, it would be brought as the תמיד.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked him. He said to them: If goat meat were better, it would be offered as the daily offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues. The king and queen ask יששכר their question, and he answers that lamb must be better, since the תמיד is a lamb.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יששכר uses the Temple service as his proof. Because the daily תמיד is a lamb, he concludes lambs are the better animal. Later steps will show this reasoning is wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: The תמיד, the daily communal offering, which is a lamb
Let it be offered (literally, let it go up on the מזבח)

phrases.english: They asked him; he said to them:
If goat were better, let it be offered as the daily offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story begun in step 7 and answers the king's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Lamb is better, because the תמיד is a lamb.

steps.title: The king has both of יששכר's hands cut off
steps.stepSummary: יששכר gestures with his hand while speaking. The king orders his right hand cut off. A bribe gets the left hand cut instead, and then the king orders the right hand cut too.
steps.simpleTranslation: As he spoke, he gestured with his hand. The king said: Since he gestured with his hand, cut off his right hand. He gave a bribe, and they cut off his left hand. The king heard and said: Let them cut off his right hand as well.
steps.whatsHappening: This finishes the answer to the question of what became of יששכר. His dismissive hand motion costs him both hands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The gesture seemed disrespectful to the king, so the king ordered the hand that made it cut off. Trying to escape with a bribe only made things worse: he lost the left hand and then the right one too.

phrases.english: While he was speaking, he gestured with his hand.
The king said to them:
Since he gestured with his hand,
cut off his right hand.
He gave a bribe,
and they cut off his left hand.
The king heard and said:
Let them cut off his right hand as well.
phrases.notes: The letters in square brackets are the corrected wording.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the story and finishes answering step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: יששכר lost both of his hands.

steps.title: רב יוסף sees fitting punishment
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף blesses ה׳ for bringing retribution on יששכר איש כפר ברקאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: Blessed is the Merciful One, who took retribution on יששכר איש כפר ברקאי.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף comments on the story. He says ה׳ gave יששכר what he deserved.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 5, יששכר wrapped his hands in silk so they would not get dirty during the עבודה. Now he loses those very hands. The punishment matches the sin of disgracing the קדשים.

keyTerms.meaning: His punishment, the retribution he deserved

steps.whatToRemember: יששכר honored his own hands over the קדשים, so he lost his hands. This is punishment that matches the sin, מדה כנגד מדה.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
Blessed is the Merciful One, who took
retribution from Yissachar of Kfar Barkai.
phrases.notes: Some versions don't have the letter in round brackets.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Comments on how the story ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Losing his hands was a just punishment for יששכר.

steps.title: רב אשי: lambs and goats are equal
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says יששכר had not learned the משנה that lambs are listed before goats, yet the two are equal.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: He had not learned what we learned in the משנה: Lambs come before goats everywhere. One might think this is because they are better. Therefore the verse says 'And if a lamb,' which teaches that both are equal.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי goes back to יששכר's answer to the king and shows it was wrong. A משנה teaches that lambs are not better than goats.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יששכר argued that lambs are better because the תמיד is a lamb. The משנה teaches that the Torah usually lists lambs before goats, but not because they are better. In the חטאת section, goat comes first and lamb comes after ("ואם כבש"), which proves the two are equal.
steps.confusionAlert: Coming first in the list does not mean being better. The משנה stresses that order does not show importance here.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי וְלָא הֲוָה תְּנֵי לֵיהּ.
phrases.english: Rav Ashi said: And he had not learned it,

phrases.aramaic: דִּתְנַן: כְּבָשִׂים קוֹדְמִין לָעִזִּים בְּכׇל מָקוֹם.
phrases.english: as we learned: Lambs come before goats everywhere.
One might think it is because they are choicer?
The verse says: "And if a lamb",
which teaches that both are equal as one.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי וְלָא הֲוָה תְּנֵי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the story to criticize the content of יששכר's answer.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: יששכר's claim that lamb is better than goat
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A משנה teaches that lambs and goats are equal. The order of the list does not show which is better.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה "כבשים קודמין לעזים" and the פסוק "ואם כבש"

steps.title: רבינא: he did not even know the פסוק
steps.stepSummary: רבינא goes further: יששכר had not even read the simple פסוקים, which say "if a lamb" and "if a goat" as equal choices.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: He had not even read the Scripture, as it is written: 'If a lamb' and 'If a goat.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא makes the criticism even sharper. You don't need a משנה to know this, because the plain פסוק already shows it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a שלמים, the Torah says "if a lamb" and "if a goat," offering them as two equal choices. So יששכר, a כהן גדול, missed something written plainly in the Torah, not only something taught in the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: The written פסוקים of the Torah

steps.whatToRemember: יששכר's answer was wrong on two levels: it goes against the משנה (רב אשי) and against the simple פסוק (רבינא).

phrases.english: Ravina said:
He had not even read the Scripture,
as it is written: "If a lamb", "If a goat".

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבִינָא אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ מִקְרָא נָמֵי לָא קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Strengthens רב אשי's criticism by showing an even more basic source.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: יששכר's claim that lamb is better than goat
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The plain פסוק lists lamb and goat as equal options.

steps.title: Torah scholars increase peace in the world
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר in the name of רבי חנינא teaches that תלמידי חכמים increase peace in the world, reading "your children" as "your builders."
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said in the name of רבי חנינא: Torah scholars increase peace in the world, as it says: 'And all your children shall be taught of ה׳, and great shall be the peace of your children.' Do not read 'your children' but 'your builders.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes with a well-known teaching of blessing. Torah scholars bring peace to the world.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק links learning Torah from ה׳ with great peace. By reading בָּנָיִךְ (your children) as בּוֹנָיִךְ (your builders), the דרשה teaches that people who learn Torah are the builders of the world, and they bring it peace.

keyTerms.meaning: Do not read it as... (a דרשה that reads a word with different vowels)

steps.whatToRemember: The section ends on a positive note: real Torah scholars build the world and spread peace.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said in the name of Rabbi Chanina:
Torah scholars increase peace in the world,
as it is stated: "And all your children shall be taught of ה׳,
and great shall be the peace of your children"
Do not read "your children" but "your builders."
phrases.notes: The words in square brackets are the corrected wording. The same letters can be read as "children" or "builders."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא: תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים מַרְבִּים שָׁלוֹם בָּעוֹלָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new, separate teaching that closes the section on a note of blessing.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תלמידי חכמים increase peace in the world, because they are the "builders."
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Torah learning builds the world and brings it peace.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing the chapter and finishing the tractate
steps.stepSummary: The traditional closing formula: we will return to you, פרק המביא אשם, and מסכת כריתות is now finished.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, chapter 'המביא אשם', and מסכת כריתות is complete.
steps.whatsHappening: This is not an argument. It is the traditional closing line that marks the end of the פרק and the end of the whole מסכת כריתות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word הדרן expresses the learner's promise to come back and review this פרק again. The added words וסליקא לה מסכת כריתות tell us this was the final פרק, so the whole מסכת is done. It comes right after רבי אלעזר's teaching about תלמידי חכמים bringing peace, which is a fitting way to finish a מסכת.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you: the closing formula said at the end of every פרק
A tractate, one volume of the תלמוד
The tractate about sins that carry the punishment of כרת

steps.whatToRemember: Finishing a מסכת is a סיום. The הדרן is a promise to come back and learn it again, not to leave it behind.

phrases.english: We will return to you, 'One who brings an אשם'
phrases.notes: 'המביא אשם' is the name of this פרק, taken from its opening words.

phrases.english: and Tractate כריתות is completed

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Formally closes the פרק and the מסכת after the final aggadic teaching in Step 13.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: פרק המביא אשם and all of מסכת כריתות are complete, with a commitment to return and review.
